exam_facts.test: CT Abdomen and Pelvis with Contrast
exam_facts.result: Parent and teacher behavioral checklists indicate patterns consistent with oppositional behaviors without conduct problems. | Normal background rhythm (dominant 8–9 Hz alpha activity posteriorly, reactive to eye opening); no epileptiform discharges, focal slowing, or paroxysmal abnormalities
No evidence of an anxiety disorder, depression, or ADHD. | Appropriate mood and affect. | Exhibits some oppositional behaviors during interview.
Well-nourished, well-groomed male in no acute distress.
Hemoglobin 13.4 g/dL, WBC 6.2 × 10³/μL, neutrophils 3.5 × 10³/μL, lymphocytes 2.1 × 10³/μL, platelets 245 × 10³/μL, no blast forms or dysplasia

Sodium 139 mmol/L, potassium 4.2 mmol/L, chloride 103 mmol/L, CO2 24 mmol/L, BUN 10 mg/dL, creatinine 0.5 mg/dL, glucose 82 mg/dL, calcium 9.4 mg/dL, ALT 18 U/L, AST 20 U/L, total protein 6.8 g/dL, albumin 4.1 g/dL
Color: pale yellow; clarity: clear; specific gravity: 1.012; pH: 6.0; no glucose, ketones, protein, blood, leukocyte esterase, or nitrites; 0–1 WBC/hpf, 0 RBC/hpf, no casts or crystals
Normal wave I–V latencies and interpeak intervals bilaterally; no evidence of retrocochlear pathology
Thresholds ≤15 dB HL across 250–8000 Hz bilaterally

Normal liver echotexture and size (right lobe 9.2 cm), patent portal vein, normal gallbladder without stones or wall thickening, normal kidneys (right 9.8 cm, left 10.1 cm), no splenomegaly or abdominal masses
Normal vertebral alignment, disc height, and marrow signal; no cord compression, syrinx, tethered cord, or intramedullary lesion; conus terminates at L1–L2 level
